la-forme-rytirska-praha.seoTitulek: La Forme Prague Old Town – bakery café & breakfast
la-forme-rytirska-praha.seoPopis: La Forme on Rytířská, steps from Old Town Square: one of Prague's best-rated bakeries with filled croissants, danishes and specialty coffee. Open from 7:30.
la-forme-rytirska-praha.popis:
La Forme is one of Prague's best-rated bakeries, and in August 2026 it opened its third and largest location right in the historic centre – on Rytířská street, a short walk from Můstek and Old Town Square. Unlike the tiny original bakery in Dejvice, here you can sit down: the café has around twenty seats and the pastries are baked on site.

Croissants, danishes and Scandinavian style

Everything is baked right here: filled croissants, playful danishes and sweet swirls, served with specialty coffee or matcha. The interior is bright and minimalist, inspired by Scandinavia.

Breakfast in the city centre

It opens at 7:30 on weekdays and at 8:00 at weekends, which makes it one of the few good options for an early breakfast in the Old Town before the crowds arrive.
la-forme-rytirska-praha.tip: Come in the morning – pastries at La Forme often sell out early. Pick a filled croissant or a danish and pair it with a flat white or matcha.

stranou-praha.seoTitulek: Stranou Prague Malá Strana – breakfast & brunch
stranou-praha.seoPopis: Stranou in Malá Strana, near Petřín funicular: cosy bistro with breakfast from 7:30, plum pancakes, creamy scrambled eggs and sourdough from Tisse Bakery.
stranou-praha.popis:
Stranou is a small bistro with a big heart on Hellichova street in Malá Strana (Lesser Town), a few minutes from Újezd and the Petřín funicular – and about ten minutes' walk from Charles Bridge. In the morning it smells of freshly baked cake and specialty coffee, and the vaulted interior is bright and cosy.

Breakfast and brunch from early morning

It opens at 7:30 on weekdays and 8:30 at weekends. The breakfast menu is served from 8:00 to 15:00 and changes with the seasons – think a bistro plate with ham off the bone or a sausage from a family butcher, fried egg, Czech hermelín cheese and sourdough from Tisse Bakery, creamy scrambled eggs with pumpkin crunch, a vegan and gluten-free savoury oat porridge or plum pancakes with quark cream and gingerbread crumble.

Lunch menu

From 11:00 to 15:00 there is also a lunch menu – soup of the day, Swedish meatballs, quesadilla or a vegan kimchi poke bowl. Gluten-free bread is available.
stranou-praha.tip: Order the creamy scrambled eggs with pumpkin crunch, or the plum pancakes with gingerbread crumble if you have a sweet tooth. A perfect stop before or after walking up Petřín Hill.

coffee-bird-praha.seoTitulek: Coffee Bird Prague – breakfast & brunch near Národní
coffee-bird-praha.seoPopis: Coffee Bird on Pštrossova, near the National Theatre: a cosy living-room style café with eggs, homemade granola, semolina porridge and French toast. Open daily.
coffee-bird-praha.popis:
Coffee Bird is a small breakfast café on Pštrossova street, right next to the well-known Globe bookstore and a short walk from the National Theatre and the Vltava riverbank. It was opened in summer 2026 by a young couple, Adéla and Bruno Kraus, and at weekends there is often a queue.

Breakfast and brunch until 14:00

The menu was created by Adéla, who previously cooked at some of Prague's favourite brunch spots, Etapa and Sestava. Expect egg dishes, homemade granola, Czech semolina porridge with chocolate and French toast with blueberry compote. Coffee comes from Doubleshot roastery, bread from Zrno Zrnko bakery, and cakes and cookies are baked on site.

Like breakfast at a friend's place

The space seats around twenty and feels like a living room: a big wooden table, retro furniture, a bookshelf and a chest of drawers with yellow drawers. There is no classic bar – staff move freely between the guests.
coffee-bird-praha.tip: Breakfast is served until 14:00. Try the semolina porridge with chocolate – a Czech childhood classic – or the French toast with blueberry compote.

kavarna-muna-praha.seoTitulek: Muna Prague – Argentine medialunas & specialty coffee
kavarna-muna-praha.seoPopis: Kavárna Muna on Myslíkova, New Town: Argentine medialunas – softer, sweeter cousins of the croissant – with specialty coffee. Open daily from 8:00.
kavarna-muna-praha.popis:
Muna on Myslíkova street brings a piece of Argentina to the centre of Prague. If you're looking for a slow morning coffee, a sweet breakfast or an afternoon break with exceptional pastries, Muna is one of the most interesting newcomers on the Prague food scene.

Argentina's answer to the croissant

The star here are medialunas – traditional Argentine pastries that look like croissants but are softer, more tender and slightly sweet. In Argentina they are part of everyday life, usually eaten with coffee at breakfast or in the afternoon. You'll find classic medialunas as well as almond or pistachio filled versions and regular seasonal specials.

Specialty coffee and a relaxed vibe

Coffee comes from Father's Coffee Roastery. In the morning it's a breakfast spot, during the day a coffee stop, and in the evening the big central table fills with Spanish wine and cava. Open every day from 8:00, with outdoor seating and dogs welcome.
kavarna-muna-praha.tip: Try a classic medialuna first, then a pistachio one. They are softer and sweeter than a French croissant – perfect with a flat white.

dabl-bistro-praha.seoTitulek: Dabl. Prague – breakfast bistro near Old Town
dabl-bistro-praha.seoPopis: Dabl. on Rybná street, behind Kotva: modern breakfast bistro with tiramisu French toast, sourdough pancakes, eggs with guanciale and a quiet courtyard.
dabl-bistro-praha.popis:
Dabl. is a modern breakfast bistro on Rybná street, just behind the Kotva department store and a few minutes' walk from Old Town Square. It opened in August 2026 and is run by the same team behind the popular Vinohrady café Laskavá. Czech tech magazine CzechCrunch called it a pleasantly non-touristy place in the middle of the tourist centre.

Sweet and savoury breakfasts

On the menu: scrambled eggs with guanciale, a chicken and kimchi sandwich, salmon with black rice, salads or sweet potato fries with hummus. Sweet tooth? Go for the tiramisu French toast or sourdough pancakes with pistachio. Drinks include their own house roast, ube and matcha lattes, lemonades, wine and cocktails.

A hidden courtyard

The pastel interior with exposed brick feels slightly industrial. The big bonus is a quiet courtyard garden, where you can escape the busy streets. Open daily from 8:00 (weekends from 9:00).
dabl-bistro-praha.tip: Order the tiramisu French toast or the sourdough pancakes with pistachio and kadaif – they taste a bit like the famous Dubai chocolate. On a sunny day, grab a table in the courtyard.

hans-coffee-praha.seoTitulek: Hans Coffee Prague – Nordic café near Republic Square
hans-coffee-praha.seoPopis: Hans Coffee on Truhlářská, near Náměstí Republiky: minimalist Scandinavian-style café with La Cabra coffee and cardamom buns from Solo bakery. Weekdays from 7:30.
hans-coffee-praha.popis:
Hans Coffee is a small Scandinavian-style café on Truhlářská street, a short walk from Náměstí Republiky (Republic Square). It is run by the founder of Prague's Solo bakery, and Forbes Czech lists it among the most stylish micro-cafés in the city centre.

Danish coffee and Nordic buns

On the grinder you'll find beans from Danish roastery La Cabra and Prague's BeBerry, served with pastries from Solo bakery – cardamom and cinnamon buns or a savoury sourdough roll. It's a place for great coffee and a sweet breakfast on the go rather than a big brunch: open weekdays only, from 7:30.

Minimalism and friendly baristas

A custom stainless-steel bar, wooden benches and a big mirror make up the interior. The baristas are happy to help you choose a coffee.
hans-coffee-praha.tip: Pair a flat white with a cardamom or cinnamon bun from Solo bakery – or the savoury sourdough roll with whipped butter and cheese. Note: closed at weekends.

mysak-prazsky-hrad.seoTitulek: Myšák Prague Castle – breakfast & Czech cakes
mysak-prazsky-hrad.seoPopis: Myšák at Prague Castle, Hradčany Square: classic Czech pastry shop with breakfast, specialty coffee and courtyard seating in the Schwarzenberg Palace.
mysak-prazsky-hrad.popis:
Myšák is a legendary Prague pastry shop, and its branch on Hradčany Square right at Prague Castle is one of the best places for breakfast near the castle. It sits in the Schwarzenberg Palace, with seating in the palace courtyard – far from the busy tourist streets.

Czech breakfast and classic cakes

The breakfast menu is built on Czech flavours, with specialty coffee and fresh pastries. Then there are the cakes Czechs grew up with: větrník (a caramel cream puff), věneček, laskonky and kremrole (cream horns), plus seasonal specials. Open daily 9:00–19:00 and you can book online or by phone.
mysak-prazsky-hrad.tip: Try the Prague egg with Prague ham and fresh horseradish – a true Czech classic. Then share a větrník, the caramel cream puff Czechs love, before heading into the castle.

sugar-life-praha.seoTitulek: Sugar Life Prague – macarons & dessert boutique
sugar-life-praha.seoPopis: Sugar Life on Těšnov, near Florenc: dessert boutique by pastry chef Vlad Ryasnyy – creative macarons, madeleines and coffee. A sweet stop, not a big brunch.
sugar-life-praha.popis:
Sugar Life is a modern dessert boutique on Těšnov street near Florenc. Behind it is pastry chef Vlad Ryasnyy, known for his precision and bold flavour combinations.

Desserts that push boundaries

The stars are macarons – but not as you know them, with flavours such as truffle or parmesan. You'll also find madeleines, custard, handmade dragées, ice cream, spreads and nougat. Desserts are not overly sweet; the focus is on flavour and texture.

A sweet stop

It works more like a pastry boutique than a classic café – perfect for coffee and something sweet. Opens at 11:00 on weekdays and 12:00 at weekends, so it's for a late sweet breakfast rather than an early start.
sugar-life-praha.tip: Get a box of macarons in unusual flavours – including savoury ones like parmesan – and a coffee. A great gift to take home, too.

pekarna-august.seoTitulek: August Prague – bakery café & croissants on Na Poříčí
pekarna-august.seoPopis: August on Na Poříčí, near Republic Square: minimalist bakery café specialising in croissants and laminated pastry, with specialty coffee and matcha.
pekarna-august.popis:
August combines a modern café, bakery and espresso bar in one clean, minimalist space on Na Poříčí street, a few steps from Náměstí Republiky. If you are looking for breakfast in central Prague built around exceptional pastry, this is the place.

All about laminated dough

August specialises in laminated dough – croissants, pain au chocolat and other layered pastries, both classic and creative versions with creams, fruit and nuts. The selection changes regularly. Pair them with specialty coffee, matcha or chai latte.

Open every day from 8:30. No reservations – just walk in.
pekarna-august.tip: Besides the croissants, try the herb omelette with parmesan – one of our favourite breakfasts in the area.

kafkoff-praha.seoTitulek: Kafkoff Prague – Sunday brunch buffet at Old Town Square
kafkoff-praha.seoPopis: Kafkoff on Franz Kafka Square, steps from Old Town Square: café with family Sunday brunch buffet, bottomless prosecco, DJ and kids' programme.
kafkoff-praha.popis:
Kafkoff is a popular café on Franz Kafka Square, literally a few steps from Old Town Square. It's a good spot for breakfast and coffee in the heart of the city, but it's best known for its Sunday event.

Brunch, Beats & Kids every Sunday

Every Sunday from 11:00 to 15:00 there's an all-you-can-eat brunch buffet with breakfast and lunch dishes – salmon tartare, hummus, a pancake and fruit bar and more – with bottomless prosecco included. A DJ plays, and kids get a bouncy castle, Montessori toys, workshops and face painting. Prices around 1,190 CZK for adults and 590 CZK for children.

Capacity is limited, so book in advance online or by phone.
kafkoff-praha.tip: On weekdays, try the sourdough bread with avocado purée. For Sunday brunch with kids, book well ahead – it fills up fast.

umamy-cafe-narodni-praha.seoTitulek: Umámy Café Prague – brunch in a courtyard on Národní
umamy-cafe-narodni-praha.seoPopis: Umámy Café on Národní street, near the National Theatre: cosy courtyard café with breakfast and brunch plates, homemade cakes and specialty coffee.
umamy-cafe-narodni-praha.popis:
Umámy Café is a cosy café hidden in a courtyard on Národní street, close to the National Theatre and the river. It feels like a quiet refuge from the busy city – a place for breakfast, brunch, a light lunch or coffee and cake.

The name plays on the flavour umami and the Czech u mámy – "at mum's place". Expect generous breakfast and brunch plates, granola, homemade pastries and cakes. It's equally good for a relaxed morning with friends or a quiet hour with a laptop. Open daily (Mon–Sat from 9:00, Sun from 10:00), dogs welcome.
umamy-cafe-narodni-praha.tip: Go for one of the savoury brunch plates with eggs and homemade bread, and finish with a slice of cake from the counter.

smetanaq-cafe-bistro-praha.seoTitulek: SmetanaQ Prague – breakfast with Vltava & castle views
smetanaq-cafe-bistro-praha.seoPopis: SmetanaQ Café & Bistro on Smetana Embankment: design café with views of the Vltava, Petřín and Prague Castle. Breakfast, Royal breakfast, cakes. Daily from 9:00.
smetanaq-cafe-bistro-praha.popis:
SmetanaQ Café & Bistro is a design café on the Smetana Embankment, right by the Vltava river, with views across to Petřín and Prague Castle – a few minutes' walk from Charles Bridge. It's part of a gallery and creative centre, popular with locals and visitors alike.

Breakfast with a view

Every morning their pastry chef bakes fresh cakes, sourdough bread and savoury treats. The menu includes breakfasts and lighter brunch options, salads, sandwiches, waffles and French toast. Specialty coffee and loose-leaf tea. Open daily from 9:00; table reservations online on weekdays only.
smetanaq-cafe-bistro-praha.tip: Really hungry? The Royal breakfast covers it all: a croissant bun with salsiccia, fried egg, bacon and cheddar sauce, plus a waffle with plum compote. Ask for a window table for the river view.

kocici-kavarna-praha.seoTitulek: Cat Café Prague Old Town – Kavárna Kočičí
kocici-kavarna-praha.seoPopis: Kavárna Kočičí on Michalská, near Old Town Square: a cat café with plant-based breakfasts, bagels, pancakes and coffee. Book a table online.
kocici-kavarna-praha.popis:
Kavárna Kočičí (literally "Cat Café") is a cat café on Michalská street, a two-minute walk from Old Town Square. Cats roam freely around the café and keep you company while you eat – a relaxed, unusual spot for a late breakfast or brunch.

Plant-based options and good coffee

The menu has a wide choice of vegan and vegetarian dishes, including gluten-free and raw treats. Coffee is freshly roasted Arabica with plant-based milks (soy, almond, coconut). Opens at 11:00 on weekdays and 10:00 at weekends.

Tip: booking online in advance is recommended. Please respect the cats' rules – they decide when they want to be petted.
kocici-kavarna-praha.tip: Order the bagel with smoked salmon or the pancakes with quark, and let a cat join you at the table.

jun-matcha-bar-praha.seoTitulek: Jun Matcha Bar Prague – matcha café near Wenceslas Square
jun-matcha-bar-praha.seoPopis: Jun Matcha Bar on Opletalova, near Wenceslas Square: specialty matcha café with Hōjicha, jasmine and strawberry matcha, matcha tiramisu and brownies.
jun-matcha-bar-praha.popis:
Jun Matcha Bar is a specialty matcha café on Opletalova street, just off the top of Wenceslas Square. Everything here revolves around matcha – from a classic creamy matcha latte to creations like Jasmine Matcha, Strawberry Cream, Mango Sticky Rice or Hōjicha matcha cream.

Desserts are just as photogenic: soft matcha tiramisu, cookies and brownies, all in fresh green aesthetics. The interior is modern and minimalist – good for a quiet break, laptop work or an Instagram photo. Open daily from 8:00 (weekends from 9:00).
jun-matcha-bar-praha.tip: You have to try the Hōjicha matcha cream – or the jasmine matcha if you prefer something lighter.

cacao-praha.seoTitulek: Cacao Prague – breakfast near the Powder Tower
cacao-praha.seoPopis: Cacao on V Celnici, steps from the Powder Tower: café with English breakfast, açaí bowls, homemade desserts, a terrace with views and a kids' corner.
cacao-praha.popis:
Cacao is a stylish café a few steps from the Powder Tower and Náměstí Republiky. It combines a café, patisserie and restaurant, and is known for its homemade desserts and ice cream.

Breakfast for every taste

The breakfast and brunch menu ranges from French croissants and an English breakfast to açaí bowls and vegan granola. The interior combines historic vaulted ceilings with modern design, and in summer there's a large terrace with views over the rooftops of Prague.

Families are welcome: there is a kids' corner downstairs and a healthy children's menu. Open daily from 8:30 (weekends 9:30).
cacao-praha.tip: Try the açaí superfood bowl with banana, coconut, homemade granola, fresh fruit and chia seeds.

chloe-cafe-praha.seoTitulek: Chloé Café Prague – pink brunch café in the centre
chloe-cafe-praha.seoPopis: Chloé Café on Senovážné náměstí: Instagram-famous pink café with avocado toast, fluffy pancakes, eggs Benedict, signature cakes and chai latte.
chloe-cafe-praha.popis:
Chloé Café is a dream for anyone who loves sweets and pretty places. This café on Senovážné náměstí, a short walk from Náměstí Republiky, is famous for its pink aesthetic and flower wall – and for beautiful desserts, colourful lemonades and breakfast plates.

On the menu: avocado toast, fluffy pancakes, eggs Benedict, signature cakes and coffee specialities. A great place for brunch with friends, a celebration or just a treat. Open daily from 9:30 (Sundays from 10:00).
chloe-cafe-praha.tip: Order their chai latte – said to be one of the best in Prague – with avocado toast and eggs on sourdough, and take a photo by the pink flower wall.

mistral-cafe-praha.seoTitulek: Mistral Café Prague – brunch near Old Town Square
mistral-cafe-praha.seoPopis: Mistral Café on Valentinská, near Old Town Square: family-friendly café with eggs Benedict on potato brioche, homemade cakes, outdoor seating and a kids' corner.
mistral-cafe-praha.popis:
Mistral Café is an elegant café a few minutes from Old Town Square, near the Rudolfinum and the Jewish Quarter. It serves generous breakfasts, brunches and light lunches made from fresh ingredients.

There's a cosy interior, outdoor seating and – rare in the Old Town – a kids' corner, which makes it a great choice for brunch with children. Expect eggs Benedict, homemade cakes, lemonades and excellent coffee. Open daily from 8:00 (weekends from 9:00); you can book by phone.
mistral-cafe-praha.tip: Go for the eggs Benedict on potato brioche with crispy bacon and hollandaise – or, for a sweet start, creamy yoghurt with gluten-free granola and raspberry compote.

pauseteria-cafe-garden-praha.seoTitulek: Pauseteria Prague – all-day brunch on Old Town Square
pauseteria-cafe-garden-praha.seoPopis: Pauseteria on Old Town Square: stylish café with all-day brunch, hashbrown Benedict with truffle, specialty coffee from Czech roasters. Open daily from 9:00.
pauseteria-cafe-garden-praha.popis:
Pauseteria is a stylish café right on Old Town Square, in the arcades of the former town hall. Unlike many cafés on the square, it focuses on real quality: breakfasts and all-day brunch made from fresh ingredients every day.

Coffee comes from two grinders, with beans from Czech specialty roasters, and they make a precise filter too. The interior is clean, cosy and well designed – a calm spot for a slow morning or an afternoon break in the centre. Open daily from 9:00; booking by phone.
pauseteria-cafe-garden-praha.tip: The hashbrown Benedict with a crispy potato base, ham off the bone and truffle is pure brunch luxury – the hollandaise brings it all together.

buddha-bar-praha.seoTitulek: Buddha-Bar Prague – Sunday brunch buffet with sushi
buddha-bar-praha.seoPopis: Buddha-Bar Prague on Jakubská, near the Powder Tower: Sunday brunch buffet (October–April) with sushi, oysters, noodle bar and desserts. Kids under 5 free.
buddha-bar-praha.popis:
Buddha-Bar Prague is an Asian fusion restaurant and sushi bar on Jakubská street in the Old Town, near the Powder Tower. It belongs to the international Buddha-Bar brand and is known for its dramatic interior with a giant Buddha statue. It's also listed in the Gault&Millau guide.

Sunday brunch, October to April

Brunch is served every Sunday from 12:00 to 16:00 during the season from October to April. It's a buffet with sushi, fresh oysters, salads, a noodle bar, international hot dishes and desserts. Soft drinks, coffee and tea are included. Around 1,599 CZK per adult, 800 CZK for children aged 6–12 and free for kids under 5, with a kids' corner. Booking recommended.
buddha-bar-praha.tip: Don't miss the sushi and fresh oysters, then the wok noodles. Book a table – Sunday brunch is popular.

traum-concept-praha.seoTitulek: Traum Concept Prague – Berlin-style brunch bistro
traum-concept-praha.seoPopis: Traum Concept in the passage between Revoluční and Benediktská: Berlin-style brunch bistro with eggs Benedict, Turkish eggs, crème brûlée French toast.
traum-concept-praha.popis:
Traum Concept (German for "dream") is a new brunch bistro in the passage between Revoluční and Benediktská streets, a few minutes from Náměstí Republiky. Its owners love unpretentious Berlin cafés – so expect raw walls, neon, industrial details and furniture like your Czech grandma's. Coffee comes from Berlin roastery 19grams.

Chefs from Eska and Michelin-listed Štangl

The kitchen is run by chefs from Prague favourites Eska and Michelin-recommended Štangl. On the menu: eggs Benedict on homemade brioche with kimchi crisps, Turkish eggs with lime labneh and chilli crunch, hashbrown with poached egg and gravlax salmon, and for dessert crème brûlée French toast with buckwheat popcorn.

Open Wed–Fri 8:00–17:30 and weekends 9:00–16:00; closed on Tuesdays, and on Mondays only coffee and cakes. No reservations.
traum-concept-praha.tip: Order the hashbrown with poached egg and gravlax, then share the crème brûlée French toast. Pair with a flat white from 19grams.

spojka-karlin.seoPopis: Spojka in Karlín, Prague: stylish bistro for breakfast and weekend brunch – eggs Benedict with gravlax, vegetarian options, specialty coffee. Book online.
spojka-karlin.popis:
Spojka captures the spirit of modern Karlín, Prague's trendiest neighbourhood just east of the centre (two metro stops from Náměstí Republiky). A stylish space, quality food and a relaxed atmosphere make it a favourite for breakfast, brunch and long catch-ups with friends.

Brunch in the heart of Karlín

The menu combines a modern approach with quality ingredients – from lighter breakfasts to hearty weekend brunch dishes, with plenty of vegetarian options. Open daily from 8:00 (weekends from 9:00) until late evening. Tables can be booked online.
spojka-karlin.tip: Try the eggs Benedict with salmon gravlax – perfectly poached eggs, homemade hollandaise and a fluffy English muffin. A brunch classic that never disappoints.

muj-salek-kavy-praha.seoTitulek: Můj šálek kávy Prague – specialty coffee & brunch, Karlín
muj-salek-kavy-praha.seoPopis: Můj šálek kávy in Karlín: one of Prague's best-known specialty coffee cafés with brunch – Turkish eggs, salsiccia plate, French toast with pears.
muj-salek-kavy-praha.popis:
Můj šálek kávy ("My cup of coffee") is one of the best-known breakfast and brunch spots in Karlín. It's part of the Doubleshot family, one of the pioneers of Prague's specialty coffee scene, so the coffee is excellent – and the brunch menu goes far beyond avocado toast.

A bold brunch menu

Recently on the menu: grilled salsiccia with bacon, fried egg, ricotta and roast potatoes, popular Turkish eggs with garlic yoghurt, chilli butter and focaccia, an omelette with Prague ham, an open sandwich with pumpkin hummus and tempeh, a chorizo bowl and French toast with caramel, pears and mascarpone. Busy at weekends – book online.
muj-salek-kavy-praha.tip: Try the open sandwich with pumpkin hummus, or the chorizo bowl. And of course a filter coffee from Doubleshot.

tea-field-praha.seoTitulek: Tea Field Prague – tea bar & matcha in Karlín
tea-field-praha.seoPopis: Tea Field in Karlín: tea bar with traditional tea ceremony, milk teas, iced tea and matcha specialities like mango matcha. A calm alternative to coffee.
tea-field-praha.popis:
Tea Field is a unique tea bar in Karlín where quality tea and the tea ritual take centre stage. It's not a café with a kitchen – the focus is on the experience of preparing tea, made right in front of you with attention to detail.

But Tea Field isn't only traditional: there are milk teas, iced teas and matcha specialities with a modern twist. Fresh flowers are sold inside, which makes the space especially pleasant. A calm alternative for anyone who prefers tea to coffee. Open daily (weekdays from 9:00, weekends from 10:00).
tea-field-praha.tip: Order the mango matcha – green matcha energy with the sweetness of mango and a perfectly smooth finish.

pleiku-coffee-praha.seoPopis: Pleiku on Zenklova street, Libeň: Vietnamese café with specialty coffee from Vietnam, egg coffee, coconut coffee and brunch dishes. Open daily from 9:00.
pleiku-coffee-praha.popis:
Pleiku is a Vietnamese café in Libeň (Prague 8), close to Karlín. It combines specialty coffee from Vietnam, traditional Vietnamese flavours and modern brunch dishes in a fresh yet authentic setting – ideal if you want to try something different from classic European coffee.

Don't miss their specialities: Vietnamese coffee with condensed milk, filter brews and other original combinations, alongside breakfast and brunch dishes inspired by Vietnamese cuisine. Open daily 9:00–19:00.
pleiku-coffee-praha.tip: Try the Vietnamese coffee with condensed milk – sweet, strong and completely different from espresso.

family-bistro-praha.seoTitulek: Family Bistro Kobylisy Prague – breakfast & lunch
family-bistro-praha.seoPopis: Family Bistro in Kobylisy, Prague 8: friendly neighbourhood bistro with fried eggs, scrambled eggs with bryndza, avocado toast and crêpes. Weekdays from 8:00.
family-bistro-praha.popis:
Family Bistro is a friendly neighbourhood bistro in Kobylisy, Prague 8 – a quieter residential area north of the centre. It serves fresh food from quality ingredients in a calm local atmosphere.

Open on weekdays from 8:00 to 15:00, it offers fried eggs, scrambled eggs with bryndza (a Slovak sheep cheese) and avocado toast with feta and tomatoes, plus a lunch menu, soups and desserts with good coffee or homemade lemonade. Closed at weekends; booking by phone.
family-bistro-praha.tip: Order the delicate crêpes filled with raspberry-mascarpone cream, forest berries, maple syrup and fresh mint.

etapa-karlin-praha.seoTitulek: Etapa Karlín Prague – seasonal brunch & sourdough
etapa-karlin-praha.seoPopis: Etapa in Karlín: seasonal vegetable-forward brunch, 100% wholegrain sourdough baked in-house, specialty coffee. Scrambled eggs with wild garlic pesto.
etapa-karlin-praha.popis:
Etapa in Karlín serves seasonal, colourful vegetable-forward dishes and drinks from local ingredients, with surprising flavours. They bake 100% wholegrain sourdough bread in-house and work with farmers from all over the country – nature and the season are the head chef here.

Add specialty coffee and homemade sweets, and you have one of Karlín's best brunch spots, especially if you like vegetarian food. Opening hours vary through the week (from 8:00 or 9:00); reservations only for the 9:00 slot.
etapa-karlin-praha.tip: Their scrambled eggs with wild garlic pesto, stracciatella and pumpkin seeds on house sourdough are excellent.

eska-karlin.seoTitulek: Eska Karlín Prague – iconic bakery & Czech brunch
eska-karlin.seoPopis: Eska in Karlín: iconic Prague bakery and restaurant with modern Czech breakfast, house sourdough, sausages and fermented lemonades. Daily from 8:00.
eska-karlin.popis:
Eska is more than a café – it's an experience and one of the icons of Prague's brunch scene. This bakery with a kitchen, in an industrial space with an open kitchen in the heart of Karlín, combines traditional Czech cooking with a modern approach, craft and sustainability.

Expect original breakfast combinations, house sourdough, seasonal ingredients and great coffee. Come hungry – whether you choose their famous sausages, scrambled eggs or a homemade Czech buchta (sweet bun), it will be worth it. Open daily from 8:00 (weekends 9:00); no reservations.
eska-karlin.tip: The Czech breakfast with soft-boiled egg, Prague ham and their "33" bread is a safe bet – pair it with a fermented lemonade.

bistro-proti-proudu-praha.seoTitulek: Proti Proudu Karlín Prague – breakfast until noon
bistro-proti-proudu-praha.seoPopis: Bistro Proti Proudu in Karlín, near Florenc: breakfast until 12:00 – Turkish eggs, English breakfast, French toast. Weekdays from 7:30.
bistro-proti-proudu-praha.popis:
Proti Proudu ("Against the Current") is a modern bistro in Karlín, two minutes from Florenc metro and bus station. It opened in 2014, inspired by Italian cafés – dense espresso, long breakfasts and a glass of prosecco. It opens at 7:30 on weekdays and 9:00 at weekends.

Breakfast until noon

Breakfast is served daily until 12:00: Turkish eggs with herb yoghurt and nut butter, an English breakfast with salsiccia, tomato beans and potato cake, cheddar omelette, fried eggs with bacon, eggs in a glass with Grana Padano and French toast with mascarpone and maple syrup. Later in the day there's pasta, salads and homemade desserts.
bistro-proti-proudu-praha.tip: Can't decide? Order the "Plate for the Indecisive" – eggs in a glass, croque-monsieur, a waffle with vanilla cream and fruit on one plate.

dvorek-karlin-praha.seoPopis: Dvorek in Karlín: relaxed bistro with weekend brunch 9–14 – big brunch plates, poached eggs, pink waffle with strawberries, matcha drinks. Book online.
dvorek-karlin-praha.popis:
Dvorek ("Little Courtyard") is a relaxed bistro on Křižíkova street in the heart of Karlín. On weekdays it serves a lunch menu to the surrounding offices; at weekends it turns into a place for a slow brunch with no alarm clock. Seasonal ingredients, specialty coffee.

Weekend brunch

Saturday and Sunday from 9:00 to 14:00 they serve a brunch that looks as good as it tastes: a big brunch plate with scrambled eggs, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon and homemade bread, poached eggs on sourdough with tomatoes, a pink waffle with strawberries, raspberries and pistachio cream, yoghurt with granola or brownie with raspberries – plus colourful matcha drinks. Book online.
dvorek-karlin-praha.tip: Come for weekend brunch and try the pink waffle with strawberries and pistachio cream. Book ahead – Saturday mornings get busy.

supernova-bakehouse-karlin-praha.seoTitulek: Supernova Bakehouse Karlín Prague – croissants & coffee
supernova-bakehouse-karlin-praha.seoPopis: Supernova Bakehouse in Karlín: modern bakery with two-tone pistachio croissants, cinnamon buns and competition-level flat white. Open daily.
supernova-bakehouse-karlin-praha.popis:
Supernova Bakehouse is a modern bakery and café on Thámova street in Karlín, famous for croissants and creative pastries baked fresh every day – two-tone pistachio croissants, salted caramel croissants with meringue or cinnamon buns with pistachio cream. The interior with a terrazzo counter and a wall of colourful boxes is made for photos.

Pair your pastry with espresso, flat white, batch brew, matcha or chai. The Karlín branch is the only one serving a Competition flat white and hand-brewed coffee. Open daily, weekdays from 8:00, weekends from 9:00.
supernova-bakehouse-karlin-praha.tip: Get a pistachio croissant or a cinnamon bun with pistachio cream and an iced strawberry matcha. Coffee lovers: don't miss the Competition flat white.

nostress-bakery-karlin-praha.seoTitulek: Nostress Bakery Karlín Prague – French breakfast
nostress-bakery-karlin-praha.seoPopis: Nostress on Karlínské náměstí: French bakery café with tartines, quiche, scrambled eggs, almond and pistachio croissants, macarons and tarts. Daily.
nostress-bakery-karlin-praha.popis:
Nostress is a French bakery and café right on Karlín Square (Karlínské náměstí). Start the day with a full breakfast or just a quick coffee and croissant, come back for lunch and again for cake in the afternoon.

French breakfast

For breakfast there are scrambled eggs, tartines – country bread with avocado, roast beef or smoked salmon – quiches and baked baguettes. Sweet options include croissants (classic, almond, pistachio or raspberry), pain suisse and fruit tarts. The counter is full of macarons, millefeuille, lemon tart and pavlova. Open every day.
nostress-bakery-karlin-praha.tip: Have a tartine with smoked salmon or avocado, then a pistachio croissant. Take home their pepper-and-truffle baguette.

the-oat-bar-praha.seoTitulek: The Oat Bar Karlín Prague – porridge & skyr bowls
the-oat-bar-praha.seoPopis: The Oat Bar in Karlín, near Křižíkova metro: sweet and savoury oat porridge from organic ingredients and Icelandic skyr bowls. Open daily from 7:00.
the-oat-bar-praha.popis:
The Oat Bar is a small bistro on Křižíkova street, near Křižíkova metro station, where everything revolves around oat porridge. It was founded by Anita from Hungary, who wanted to reinvent boring childhood porridge into food that's healthy and tasty. Organic ingredients and wholegrain oat groats.

Open daily from 7:00. Sweet bowls include peanut butter, banana and chocolate, strawberry jam with roasted peanuts or classic butter, brown sugar and raisins. Savoury ones surprise: goat cheese, beetroot and pistachio, or Tex-Mex with bacon, cheddar and guacamole. Plus Icelandic skyr bowls. Few seats – most people take it to go.
the-oat-bar-praha.tip: Try the porridge with peanut butter, banana and chocolate, or the PB&J with strawberry jam. Feeling savoury? Goat cheese, beetroot and pistachio.

cafe-v-raji-praha.seoTitulek: Café V Ráji Karlín Prague – brunch & live music
cafe-v-raji-praha.seoPopis: Café V Ráji on Karlín Square: family-run Art Nouveau café with daily brunch, salmon toast, marinated eggs, matcha and live jazz on Friday evenings.
cafe-v-raji-praha.popis:
Café V Ráji ("In Paradise") is a family-run café in Art Nouveau style right on Karlín Square. By day it's a calm place for breakfast, work or a meeting; in the evening it becomes a lively meeting place with concerts by the piano – classical on Wednesdays, jazz on Fridays.

Brunch every day

The brunch menu is served weekdays 8:00–13:00 and weekends 10:00–14:00: sourdough toast with smoked salmon, dill cream, pickled onion and poached egg, marinated eggs in herb yoghurt with chilli oil, or a nut spread with homemade bread. Specialty coffee, several kinds of matcha latte and homemade desserts.
cafe-v-raji-praha.tip: Order the sourdough toast with smoked salmon and poached egg plus a matcha latte. On Friday evening, stay for the jazz.

und-kaffee-praha.seoTitulek: Ünd Kaffee Prague – bakery & laminated pastry, Letná
und-kaffee-praha.seoPopis: Ünd on Veletržní, Letná: bakery and café by the founders of Gemüse Corner – croissants, cardamom swirls and Nordic-inspired pastry. Open daily from 8:00.
und-kaffee-praha.popis:
Ünd is a bakery and café on Veletržní street between Letná and Holešovice, opened by the duo behind Gemüse Corner – one of Prague's favourite kebab spots. This time they went in a different direction: quality pastry, specialty coffee and Nordic inspiration.

The focus is on laminated pastry, one of the biggest trends in modern baking: perfectly layered croissants, cardamom swirls, cinnamon specialities and seasonal pastries. Open every day from 8:00, a short walk from the National Gallery's Trade Fair Palace.
und-kaffee-praha.tip: Try not just the classic croissant but also the modern versions filled with pistachio cream or seasonal fruit – and a cardamom swirl to go.

cafe-letka-praha.seoTitulek: Café Letka Prague – breakfast in Letná
cafe-letka-praha.seoPopis: Café Letka on Letohradská, near Letná Park: cosy café with eggs, granola, French toast with poached pear, Five Elephant coffee. Open daily from 8:00.
cafe-letka-praha.popis:
Café Letka is a cosy, much-loved café on Letohradská street in Letná, a couple of minutes from Letná Park and its famous view over Prague's bridges. It combines a friendly atmosphere with good food and drinks.

Mornings bring a great breakfast – from classic eggs and granola to sweet pastries and homemade cakes – with carefully prepared specialty coffee from Berlin's Five Elephant roastery or lemonades. During the day there's a relaxed brunch menu with sweet and savoury dishes. Open daily from 8:00 (weekends from 9:00) until late.
cafe-letka-praha.tip: The French toast with apple purée, poached pear, crème fraîche, crumble and brown butter is outstanding. Then walk to the Letná Park viewpoint.

mama-shelter-praha.seoTitulek: Mama Shelter Prague – Sunday brunch buffet
mama-shelter-praha.seoPopis: Mama Shelter Prague in Holešovice: famous all-you-can-eat Mama Brunch every Sunday 12–15 with welcome drink, in a colourful hotel restaurant.
mama-shelter-praha.popis:
Mama Shelter Prague, the colourful design hotel in Holešovice, hosts its legendary Mama Brunch every Sunday from 12:00 to 15:00 in the hotel's main restaurant.

The brunch package (around 990 CZK) includes an all-you-can-eat buffet, a welcome drink and soft drinks from the buffet (water, juice, iced tea). The buffet changes with the seasons and mixes Czech flavours with international dishes and plenty of desserts – a relaxed, informal Sunday with friends or family. Booking by phone recommended.
mama-shelter-praha.tip: Come hungry and take your time – the dessert table alone is worth it. Book ahead for Sundays.

matilda-praha.seoTitulek: Matilda Prague – Italian breakfast & brunch, Letná
matilda-praha.seoPopis: Matilda on Korunovační, Letná: Italian café and bistro with maritozzi, espresso, cacio e pepe scrambled eggs and fresh pasta. Closed Mondays.
matilda-praha.popis:
Matilda is an Italian-style café and bistro on Korunovační street in Letná. Mornings smell of freshly made maritozzi (Roman cream buns) and espresso, tables fill with breakfast plates, and at lunch there's fresh pasta, bigoli or gnocchi.

In the afternoon you can sit in the garden; in the evening it becomes a calm place for dinner with wine and tiramisu – an Italian feeling in the middle of Prague. The chef uses fresh Italian and local ingredients. Open Tue–Sun (Sunday until 16:00), closed on Mondays; book online.
matilda-praha.tip: Order the uova strapazzate cacio e pepe – soft scrambled eggs with pecorino, brown butter, fresh pepper and focaccia. Simply brilliant.

vnitroblock-praha.seoTitulek: Vnitroblock Holešovice Prague – brunch & coffee roastery
vnitroblock-praha.seoPopis: Vnitroblock in Holešovice: industrial café in a former factory with its own roastery and Skýva bakery. Weekend brunch 9–15, eggs with black truffle.
vnitroblock-praha.popis:
Vnitroblock is a multi-purpose space in a former factory between Tusarova and Dělnická streets in Holešovice – an industrial hall with brick walls, a plant-filled gallery and comfy armchairs and sofas. There's a café, restaurant, its own coffee roastery Not Another Boring Roastery and Skýva bakery. In summer you can sit in the garden under fairy lights.

Breakfast and weekend brunch

Breakfast is served weekdays 9:00–11:00 and weekends 9:00–15:00: farm scrambled eggs with fresh black truffle and whipped brown butter, Turkish eggs with Greek yoghurt, an omelette with wild garlic cheese, pea-camole bread with a 63° egg or blueberry pancakes with vanilla cream. Gluten-free bread available.
vnitroblock-praha.tip: Have the farm scrambled eggs with black truffle and Skýva sourdough. At weekends, come for brunch – and in summer, sit in the garden.

phills-corner-praha.seoTitulek: Phill's Corner Holešovice Prague – breakfast from 7:30
phills-corner-praha.seoPopis: Phill's Corner in Holešovice, near Prague Market: breakfast from 7:30 – super pancake with salmon, eggs in a glass, waffles with bacon, porridge.
phills-corner-praha.popis:
Phill's Corner is a bistro and café on the corner of Komunardů and Dělnická streets, one of the busiest crossroads in Holešovice, a few steps from the tram and Prague Market (Pražská tržnice). Their motto is simple: mornings are for breakfast.

Breakfast from 7:30, brunch at weekends

It opens at 7:30 on weekdays and 9:00 at weekends, with extra brunch specials on weekends. The menu includes the Super pancake with herb crème fraîche, smoked salmon, avocado and fried egg, three eggs in a glass with hollandaise, scrambled eggs with cheese toast and portobello, oat porridge with roasted peaches and pecans, granola with baked apple and salted caramel and waffles with bacon and maple syrup.
phills-corner-praha.tip: Order the waffles with bacon, fried eggs and maple syrup – or the Super pancake with salmon and avocado. Add an iced strawberry matcha.

kafe-francin-praha.seoTitulek: Kafe Francin Holešovice Prague – breakfast & roastery
kafe-francin-praha.seoPopis: Kafe Francin in Holešovice, near the Trade Fair Palace: café with its own roastery, English breakfast, open sandwich with eggs, croque madame. From 7:30.
kafe-francin-praha.popis:
Kafe Francin is a popular café and roastery on Dukelských hrdinů street, close to Strossmayerovo náměstí and the National Gallery's Trade Fair Palace. They roast their own coffee, which you can also buy to take home. Locals love it for its relaxed vibe, honest breakfasts and great value.

It opens at 7:30 on weekdays and 8:00 at weekends. Breakfast includes an English breakfast, an open sandwich with fried eggs, lemon ricotta and courgette, an omelette with salad, croque madame, halloumi and avocado bagel or BLT bagel, plus Greek yoghurt with granola and vegan millet porridge.
kafe-francin-praha.tip: Try the open sandwich with fried eggs, lemon ricotta and courgette, or the full English breakfast – with coffee from their own roastery.

la-forme-holesovice-praha.seoTitulek: La Forme Holešovice Prague – breakfast & croissants
la-forme-holesovice-praha.seoPopis: La Forme in Holešovice: one of Prague's best bakeries with a café – French toast with peaches, quark pancakes, scrambled eggs and filled croissants.
la-forme-holesovice-praha.popis:
La Forme is one of Prague's best-rated bakeries, and its café on Tusarova street in Holešovice is a lovely place for breakfast – inside or on the sunny terrace. Like the Old Town branch, it offers filled croissants, danishes and sweet swirls from its own bakery, plus specialty coffee.

There are also hot breakfasts: French toast with caramelised peaches, quark pancakes with plum jam and yoghurt, creamy scrambled eggs with sourdough, eggs with roasted tomatoes and porridge with cherries and hazelnuts. Open weekdays from 7:30, weekends from 8:00.
la-forme-holesovice-praha.tip: Order the French toast with caramelised peaches or the quark pancakes with plum jam – and take an almond croissant to go.

yaki-pan-praha.seoTitulek: Yaki-Pan Prague – Japanese bakery near Újezd
yaki-pan-praha.seoPopis: Yaki-Pan on Mělnická street near Újezd: Japanese bakery and brunch spot with sweet buns filled with black rice, purple sweet potato or bean paste, and matcha.
yaki-pan-praha.popis:
Yaki-Pan is a Japanese bakery and brunch spot on Mělnická street near Újezd, at the foot of Petřín Hill. It brings a very different kind of pastry to Prague – from unusual sweet buns to modern brunch sandwiches and matcha specialities. The name literally means "baked bread".

The owners, Hoan and Duy, wanted to bring Japanese baking, still little known in Europe, to Prague. Hoan even trained with a renowned Japanese baker. Open daily 10:00–18:00.
yaki-pan-praha.tip: Try the buns filled with sweet black rice, purple sweet potato or red bean paste, with a matcha latte.

dim-sum-spot-pub-andel.seoTitulek: Dim Sum Spot Anděl Prague – dim sum brunch
dim-sum-spot-pub-andel.seoPopis: Dim Sum Spot & Pub at Anděl, Smíchov: Asian dumplings, light hot dishes and sharing plates – a different kind of late breakfast, with a courtyard terrace.
dim-sum-spot-pub-andel.popis:
Dim Sum Spot & Pub at Anděl is an unusual tip for a late breakfast or brunch in Prague if you fancy something other than eggs and croissants. It combines Asian food with a relaxed pub atmosphere, serving dim sum dumplings, light hot dishes and sharing plates.

Dim sum are perfect for a late morning – light, full of flavour and made for sharing, with tea, coffee or soft drinks. There's also outdoor seating in the courtyard. Opens at 11:00 daily; book online.
dim-sum-spot-pub-andel.tip: Order a few baskets of dim sum to share. The place was founded by three friends inspired by Asian street food on their travels.

kavarna-co-hleda-jmeno-praha.seoTitulek: Kavárna co hledá jméno Prague – brunch in Smíchov
kavarna-co-hleda-jmeno-praha.seoPopis: Kavárna co hledá jméno in Smíchov, near Anděl: creative brunch with eggs Benedict soufflé, Monte Cristo sandwich, apple pancakes. Daily from 8:00.
kavarna-co-hleda-jmeno-praha.popis:
Kavárna co hledá jméno ("The café looking for a name") in Smíchov, near Anděl, is a favourite for quality coffee and creative brunch. Expect specialty coffee, honest breakfasts and homemade desserts.

On the menu: eggs Benedict soufflé, eggs Florentine soufflé, a Monte Cristo sandwich, avocado and salmon sandwich or apple pancakes. A relaxed vibe and modern design make it great for an everyday visit or a weekend brunch with friends. Open daily from 8:00; book online.
kavarna-co-hleda-jmeno-praha.tip: The eggs Benedict soufflé is an elegant twist on the classic – light, airy and finished with hollandaise. Brunch with a fine-dining touch.

cafe-peron-praha.seoTitulek: Café Perón Anděl Prague – breakfast & cakes
cafe-peron-praha.seoPopis: Café Perón on Stroupežnického, near Anděl: Italian coffee, breakfast 9–13 with brioches, avocado sourdough and homemade cakes. Courtyard garden.
cafe-peron-praha.popis:
Café Perón is a stylish café on Stroupežnického street, close to Anděl. It serves traditional Italian coffee, breakfasts and homemade cakes baked on site. In summer you can sit in the courtyard garden.

The breakfast menu is served daily 9:00–13:00: brioches with scrambled eggs and bacon, with avocado and poached egg or with smoked salmon, avocado sourdough toast, Toast Madame Perón baked in egg, scrambled eggs with spring onion, sausages with horseradish or homemade granola with yoghurt and honey.
cafe-peron-praha.tip: Savoury: brioche with avocado and poached egg or Toast Madame Perón with cheddar and bacon. Sweet: homemade granola with yoghurt and honey.

55-bakery-praha.seoPopis: 55 Bakery on Štefánikova, Smíchov: bakery café with pistachio croissants, cinnamon rolls, savoury pain suisse and sourdough. Open daily from 7:00.
55-bakery-praha.popis:
55 Bakery is a bakery and café on Štefánikova street in Smíchov, a few minutes from Anděl. Every morning they bake sourdough bread, black wheat bread, focaccia, ciabatta, baguettes, croissants and other sweet and savoury pastries.

Open every day from 7:00 to 19:00 – great for a quick breakfast on the way or a weekend morning. Highlights: pistachio croissant, a bow with coconut cream, mango and passion fruit, cinnamon roll with brown butter cream and a savoury pain suisse with figs, goat cheese and mortadella. Specialty coffee too.
55-bakery-praha.tip: Try the pistachio croissant or the cinnamon roll with brown butter cream. Savoury? The pain suisse with figs, goat cheese and mortadella.

yorkmut-cafe-praha.seoTitulek: Yorkmut Café Prague – dog café in Vinohrady
yorkmut-cafe-praha.seoPopis: Yorkmut Café on Londýnská, near I. P. Pavlova: a dog café where friendly resident dogs keep you company over coffee, fresh pastry and baked sandwiches.
yorkmut-cafe-praha.popis:
Yorkmut Café is a dog café on Londýnská street in Vinohrady, a short walk from I. P. Pavlova. Several resident dogs welcome guests – well socialised, cuddly and keen on human attention. A dog assistant looks after their wellbeing the whole time, so the visit is relaxed and safe for everyone.

Besides plenty of cuddles, you'll get good coffee, fresh pastries, homemade desserts and their popular baked open sandwiches. Open daily 10:00–13:00 and 14:00–19:00 (the dogs take a lunch break); booking online is recommended.
yorkmut-cafe-praha.tip: Have a coffee with the dogs and pick something from the daily pastry and dessert selection – the baked sandwiches make a filling, easy breakfast.

meme-brunch-praha.seoTitulek: Mèmè & Brunch Prague – brunch café in Vinohrady
meme-brunch-praha.seoPopis: Mèmè & Brunch on Slavíkova, near Jiřího z Poděbrad: stylish brunch café with hearty plates, specialty coffee and black sesame matcha latte. Daily from 9:00.
meme-brunch-praha.popis:
Mèmè & Brunch is a modern, stylish café and brunch spot on Slavíkova street, a few steps from Náměstí Jiřího z Poděbrad. It quickly won over locals and visitors with its friendly concept, quality ingredients and generous brunch plates.

The menu combines brunch classics with creative twists, freshly prepared dishes and specialty coffee – ideal for a slow weekend morning with friends or a quiet breakfast before work. Open daily from 9:00 (Wednesday until 17:00, otherwise until 19:00); booking by phone.
meme-brunch-praha.tip: Try the matcha latte with black sesame cream – perfectly creamy, slightly nutty and addictively good.

o-mai-coffee-brunch-praha.seoPopis: O-Mai Coffee & Brunch on Belgická, Vinohrady: stylish café for slow breakfasts – avocado toast with salmon, vegetarian options and creative matcha drinks.
o-mai-coffee-brunch-praha.popis:
O-Mai Coffee & Brunch is a stylish café on Belgická street in Vinohrady, close to Náměstí Míru, combining a modern atmosphere with honest flavours. It's made for slow breakfasts and weekend brunch with friends.

Expect excellent avocado toasts, homemade desserts and plenty of vegetarian options. Matcha fans are well served too – prepared carefully as a classic latte or in original drinks. Open Tue–Sun 9:00–17:00, closed on Mondays; phone bookings only at weekends and on public holidays.
o-mai-coffee-brunch-praha.tip: Order the iced mango matcha, the avocado toast with salmon or the house Ô-mai breakfast.

bistro-cafe-laskava.seoTitulek: Laskavá Prague – all-day breakfast café in Vinohrady
bistro-cafe-laskava.seoPopis: Bistro Café Laskavá on Anglická, near Náměstí Míru: cosy café with all-day breakfast and brunch, eggs in a glass, croque monsieur and a courtyard garden.
bistro-cafe-laskava.popis:
Bistro Café Laskavá is a cosy café and bistro on Anglická street in Vinohrady, a few minutes from Náměstí Míru. It's a favourite with breakfast lovers – breakfast and brunch are served all day.

The interior is romantic and homely, with brick walls, wooden benches and cushions. In summer there's a quiet courtyard garden. The menu changes regularly and offers a wide range of breakfast and brunch dishes. Open weekdays from 8:00, weekends from 9:00 (Sunday until 17:00); book by phone. The same team runs Dabl. in the Old Town.
bistro-cafe-laskava.tip: Go for the Woody brunch: two eggs in a glass with chives and parmesan, croque monsieur, a seed salad and sweet buns with vanilla custard and a drop of rum.

tisse-bakery-praha.seoTitulek: TISSE Bakery Prague – craft bakery & brunch, Vinohrady
tisse-bakery-praha.seoPopis: TISSE Bakery on Krkonošská, Vinohrady: craft bakery café with slow-fermented bread, pistachio croissants, vegan pastry and brunch. Open daily from 8:00.
tisse-bakery-praha.popis:
TISSE is a craft bakery and café on Krkonošská street in Vinohrady, near Náměstí Jiřího z Poděbrad. It combines slow dough fermentation with a passion for traditional baking – every loaf takes the time it needs.

Take a fresh loaf home or stay for coffee: TISSE serves great breakfasts and brunch, including a wide choice of vegan pastries and dishes. Open weekdays from 8:00 and weekends from 8:30, until 18:00; booking by phone.
tisse-bakery-praha.tip: Don't miss the pistachio croissant – pair it with an iced matcha latte for the perfect brunch.

srnky-americka-praha.seoTitulek: Srnky Americká Prague – all-day brunch near Náměstí Míru
srnky-americka-praha.seoPopis: Srnky on Americká, Vinohrady: all-day brunch bistro famous for its Czech pancakes (lívance), farm ingredients and dog-friendly vibe. Weekdays from 7:30.
srnky-americka-praha.popis:
Srnky Americká is a café and bistro in Vinohrady, the third branch of the popular Mezi Srnky concept. It sits on Americká street, a few minutes' walk from Náměstí Míru, and has around fifty seats. Dogs are welcome.

All-day brunch

Srnky is known for all-day brunch. According to Forbes Czech, people come mainly for the famous lívance (thick Czech pancakes), but there are also unusual "breakfasts" like lečo (pepper and tomato stew), a Dutch-style schnitzel or rice pudding. No ready-made products: everything is cooked in-house from local farm ingredients. Open weekdays 7:30–20:00, weekends 8:30–17:00.
srnky-americka-praha.tip: Try the famous lívance, or something from the unusual all-day breakfasts – such as lečo or rice pudding.

foyer-cafe-praha.seoTitulek: Foyer Café Prague – Art Nouveau café at the main station
foyer-cafe-praha.seoPopis: Foyer Café in the Art Nouveau Fanta Building of Prague Main Station: croissants, pain au chocolat and coffee from 8:00, afternoon tea, views of the trains.
foyer-cafe-praha.popis:
Foyer Café is a café in the Art Nouveau Fanta Building of Prague Main Railway Station, one of the most important Art Nouveau buildings in the country. Modern elegance meets historic stucco and tall windows from which you can watch the trains depart. It is run by Spojka Events.

Morning viennoiserie and coffee

Open every day from 8:00. Mornings belong to viennoiserie – croissants, pain au chocolat or flan – and coffee, with cakes and savoury canapés in the display. It's an ideal place for breakfast before a train or after arriving in Prague. In the afternoon you can book a five o'clock tea with a tiered stand of treats.
foyer-cafe-praha.tip: Come for a morning croissant or pain au chocolat with coffee and a view of departing trains. For the afternoon, book the five o'clock tea.

pomalu-pomalu-praha.seoTitulek: Pomalu pomalu Prague – all-day bistro & bakery
pomalu-pomalu-praha.seoPopis: Pomalu pomalu on Slavíkova, near Jiřího z Poděbrad: all-day bistro from the Kin & K Bakery team – sourdough, cardamom knots and seasonal breakfast plates.
pomalu-pomalu-praha.popis:
Pomalu pomalu ("slowly, slowly") is an all-day bistro on the corner of Slavíkova and Ondříčkova streets, a few steps from Náměstí Jiřího z Poděbrad. It opened in autumn 2026, from the team behind Kin & K Bakery led by Haitham Al-Shoriym, who also founded the Tribes of Mokha roastery.

Pastry, coffee and brunch

The pastry comes from their own Kin & K bakery, which also supplies well-known Prague cafés such as Slavia, Louvre and SmetanaQ. For breakfast: bread with quark and egg or stracciatella with plums and peaches. Open weekdays from 8:00 and weekends from 9:00; Wednesday to Saturday also in the evening.
pomalu-pomalu-praha.tip: For breakfast, try bread with quark and egg or stracciatella with plums, peaches and shiso – and don't skip the famous cardamom knots from Kin & K.

cafefin-praha.seoTitulek: Cafefin Prague – brunch on Jiřího z Poděbrad square
cafefin-praha.seoPopis: Cafefin on Náměstí Jiřího z Poděbrad: popular brunch café with shakshuka, toasts with figs or burrata, Vietnamese touches and great coffee. Daily from 9:00.
cafefin-praha.popis:
Cafefin, right on Náměstí Jiřího z Poděbrad (next to the striking Church of the Sacred Heart), is a small culinary gem combining great coffee, quality food and a relaxed atmosphere. It's one of the best-known brunch addresses in Prague.

The menu goes from classic eggs and toast to shakshuka and gourmet toasts with figs or burrata, with a few Vietnamese touches from the owners. Open daily from 9:00 (until 20:00, Sundays 19:00); booking by phone recommended at weekends.
cafefin-praha.tip: The oat porridge with caramelised banana is heavenly!

soma-praha.seoTitulek: SOMA Prague – specialty coffee & brunch in Žižkov
soma-praha.seoPopis: SOMA on Seifertova, Žižkov: bright café with specialty coffee from Czech and European roasters and a seasonal brunch menu. Pumpkin bread is a must.
soma-praha.popis:
SOMA is a café on Seifertova street in Žižkov, a short walk from the main station and the Žižkov TV Tower. It combines a love of specialty coffee, honest food and slow mornings in a bright, open interior with comfy corners to relax or work.

Coffee is one of the stars: SOMA works with several respected roasters from the Czech Republic and Europe. The brunch menu changes with the seasons. Open weekdays from 8:00, weekends from 9:00, until 18:00; book online.
soma-praha.tip: The pumpkin bread with cream cheese frosting is the top pick!

sensu-cafe-praha.seoTitulek: Sensu Cafe Prague – matcha café & desserts
sensu-cafe-praha.seoPopis: Sensu Cafe near Želivského metro: modern Asian café specialising in matcha – iced matcha latte, cloud foam latte, yuzu lemonade and matcha cakes.
sensu-cafe-praha.popis:
Sensu Cafe is a modern Asian café near Želivského metro station that specialises in matcha. You'll find hot and iced matcha lattes, matcha cloud foam latte and refreshing matcha yuzu lemonade, along with homemade matcha desserts.

There's a wide choice of plant-based milks, a modern design and friendly staff. Open daily (Monday from 10:00, otherwise from 9:00) until 19:00; no reservations.
sensu-cafe-praha.tip: Iced matcha latte with vanilla cloud and oat milk is a hit – with a slice of matcha cake.

antoninovo-pekarstvi.seoTitulek: Antonínovo pekařství Prague – bakery near Jiřího z Poděbrad
antoninovo-pekarstvi.seoPopis: Antonínovo pekařství on Laubova, near Jiřího z Poděbrad: traditional Czech bakery with breakfast, poppy seed cake, gingerbread and outdoor seating. Daily from 7:00.
antoninovo-pekarstvi.popis:
Antonínovo pekařství (Antonín's Bakery) on Laubova street, just off Náměstí Jiřího z Poděbrad, is known for its tradition and excellent pastry baked from quality ingredients.

Besides fresh bread and pastry, there are tasty breakfasts and brunch treats and coffee, plus outdoor seating for spring and summer. It's a great place to try classic Czech baking. Open every day 7:00–19:30.
antoninovo-pekarstvi.tip: Try the buckwheat carrot cake, makovec (poppy seed cake) or homemade perník (gingerbread). Sporty? Go for the crunchy protein baguette.

spizirna-1902-praha.seoPopis: Spižírna 1902 on Korunní, Vinohrady: café, bistro and bakery with weekday breakfast from 8:00 and weekend brunch 9–16, seasonal menu and homemade cakes.
spizirna-1902-praha.popis:
Spižírna 1902 ("the pantry") is a café, bistro and bakery on Korunní street on the border of Vinohrady and Žižkov, near Náměstí Jiřího z Poděbrad. Trams 10 and 16 stop nearby (Perunova and Vinohradská vodárna). The idea is simple: fresh, healthy food made on site.

Breakfast on weekdays, brunch at weekends

Breakfast is served on weekdays 8:00–11:15, weekend brunch 9:00–16:00 (last orders 15:45). The menu changes with the seasons – from eggs and savoury plates to fruit bowls and sweet pancakes. Online booking on weekdays only.
spizirna-1902-praha.tip: For weekend brunch, arrive right at 9:00 – no reservations at weekends. Add a homemade bun or cake from their bakery.

dobroteka-zizkov-praha.seoTitulek: Dobrotéka Prague – breakfast café & deli in Žižkov
dobroteka-zizkov-praha.seoPopis: Dobrotéka on Hartigova, Žižkov: café and deli with specialty coffee, croissants, granola and homemade cakes, budget-friendly brunch until 13:00 and a garden.
dobroteka-zizkov-praha.popis:
Dobrotéka is a café and delicatessen on Hartigova street in Žižkov. In the morning it's a breakfast café, in the evening a pleasant place for a glass of wine. There's also a small shop with delicacies, premium cheeses and charcuterie.

Breakfast and brunch

It opens at 8:30 on weekdays and 9:00 at weekends. Breakfast means specialty coffee, loose-leaf tea, croissants, sandwiches, granola with yoghurt and fruit and homemade cakes. According to the Around Prague guide, Dobrotéka's brunch is among the most affordable in Prague; it's served until 13:00. In good weather, sit in the covered garden.
dobroteka-zizkov-praha.tip: Have granola with yoghurt and fresh fruit or a croissant with specialty coffee, and in summer sit in the covered garden. Brunch is served until 13:00.

seiferts-brunch-praha.seoTitulek: Seifert's Brunch Prague – Czech-style brunch in Žižkov
seiferts-brunch-praha.seoPopis: Seifert's Brunch on Hartigova, Žižkov: family bistro with daily Czech-style brunch – eggs, Prague ham, Blaťácké zlato cheese and Bread Society sourdough.
seiferts-brunch-praha.popis:
Seifert's Brunch is a small family bistro on Hartigova street in Žižkov. It's named after the Seifert Residence it sits in, and the design is inspired by the Czech avant-garde era when poet and Nobel laureate Jaroslav Seifert began writing. Filip and Terra Kasal opened it with their friend Tereza Ryšavá because Žižkov lacked proper brunch.

Czech brunch every day

Brunch is served on weekdays 8:00–16:00 and weekends 9:00–18:00. CzechCrunch called the menu "as Czech as it gets": eggs, Prague ham from the butcher next door, Blaťácké zlato cheese, kale and sourdough from Bread Society.
seiferts-brunch-praha.tip: Order the Czech breakfast plate with eggs, Prague ham, Blaťácké zlato cheese and Bread Society sourdough. For something sweet, don't miss the homemade buchta or gingerbread.

sladka-cesta-praha.seoTitulek: Sladká cesta Prague – all-day breakfast & bagels, Žižkov
sladka-cesta-praha.seoPopis: Sladká cesta on Hartigova, Žižkov: cosy café baking its own bagels, brioches and cakes, all-day breakfast from 7:00 on weekdays, from 69 CZK. Dogs welcome.
sladka-cesta-praha.popis:
Sladká cesta ("Sweet Way") is a cosy café and bistro on Hartigova street in Žižkov. Every day they bake their own bagels, brioches, homemade cakes and Czech yeast koláče. Dogs are welcome.

All-day breakfast

Breakfast is served all day – it opens at 7:00 on weekdays and 9:00 at weekends. Choose from eggs your way (scrambled with bacon or with mozzarella), house-baked bagels (salmon, prosciutto, Caesar), filled brioches, toasties, pancakes, yoghurt or koláče. Breakfast starts at just 69 CZK for a koláč – great value in Prague.
sladka-cesta-praha.tip: Get a bagel from their own bakery – salmon is the favourite – or scrambled eggs with bacon. For something sweet, a homemade crumble koláč from 69 CZK.

antoninova-kavarna-praha.seoTitulek: Antonínova kavárna Prague – bakery café in Vršovice
antoninova-kavarna-praha.seoPopis: Antonínova kavárna on Košická, Vršovice: calm neighbourhood café of Antonín's Bakery with pastry, cakes, matcha and gluten-free salmon toast. Daily from 8:00.
antoninova-kavarna-praha.popis:
Antonínova kavárna is the quiet café of Prague's much-loved Antonínovo pekařství bakery chain, on Košická street in Vršovice. While the bakeries are known for crusty bread, koláče, buchty and soups, the café lets you enjoy these treats on the spot in a relaxed setting.

Compared with the busy bakeries, it feels like a calm neighbourhood place: freshly roasted coffee, matcha, tea or homemade lemonade with pastry or cake. Open every day 8:00–19:30; booking by phone.
antoninova-kavarna-praha.tip: Try Antonín's gluten-free toast with smoked salmon, cheese spread, fresh lemon and dill!

sestava-vrsovice.seoTitulek: Sestava Vršovice Prague – café, roastery & breakfast
sestava-vrsovice.seoPopis: Sestava on Žitomírská, Vršovice: neighbourhood café and roastery by six friends – eggs, Czech pancakes, hummus, sourdough toasts. Weekdays from 7:00.
sestava-vrsovice.popis:
Sestava is a neighbourhood café and roastery in Vršovice, started by a group of six friends who wanted a place with a friendly atmosphere, good coffee and honest food.

They roast their own coffee and make fresh pastry, homemade syrups, breakfasts, brunch and a seasonal menu built on quality ingredients and simple, tasty dishes – breakfast eggs, lívance (Czech pancakes), hummus or combinations on sourdough. The space is designed for a community feel. Open weekdays from 7:00, weekends from 8:00.
sestava-vrsovice.tip: The lemon loaf with vanilla cream is excellent.

bistro-b-praha.seoTitulek: Bistro B Prague – breakfast at Budějovická metro
bistro-b-praha.seoPopis: Bistro B right at Budějovická metro, Prague 4: early breakfast from 7:00 – eggs Benedict, herb omelette, pea-camole toast, Not Another Boring Roastery coffee.
bistro-b-praha.popis:
Bistro B is a modern bistro and café right at the Budějovická metro exit (line C) in Prague 4 – a good choice for breakfast, brunch and specialty coffee from early morning.

The focus is on a quality morning menu: eggs Benedict, scrambled eggs, a herb omelette or granola with yoghurt and fruit, with coffee from Not Another Boring Roastery. The relaxed interior also works for a quick lunch or fresh pastry. Open weekdays from 7:00 (Friday until 15:00), closed at weekends; book online.
bistro-b-praha.tip: Order the pea-camole toast: peas, a 63° egg, pickled vegetables and toasted sourdough. It's as colourful as it is good!

flat-cafe-praha.seoTitulek: FLAT Café Prague – British-style brunch in Vršovice
flat-cafe-praha.seoPopis: FLAT on Kodaňská, Vršovice: café styled like a British living room – proper English breakfast (also vegan), pancakes and Square Mile coffee from London.
flat-cafe-praha.popis:
FLAT is a café in Vršovice on the corner of Kodaňská and Moskevská streets, furnished like a British living room – with a portrait of the Queen, a brick wall, Chesterfield sofas and antique furniture. Coffee, brunch and drinks are served "under the kind supervision of Her Majesty".

Where breakfast meets lunch

The owners say there's no line between breakfast and brunch here, so take your time. On the menu: a proper English breakfast (also in a vegan version), omelettes, toasts and pancakes. Coffee comes from London's award-winning Square Mile roastery. In the evening it's all about gin. Open weekdays from 8:30, weekends from 9:00; bookings on weekdays only.
flat-cafe-praha.tip: Come for a proper English breakfast – there's a vegan version too – or the naughty pancakes, with a slice of cake and Square Mile coffee.

vila-63-praha.seoTitulek: Vila 63 Prague – café in a 1920s villa with garden
vila-63-praha.seoPopis: Vila 63 on the Vinohrady–Vršovice border: café in a 1920s villa with a garden and Czech breakfasts – ham and eggs, sausages with horseradish. Wed–Sun.
vila-63-praha.popis:
Vila 63 is a café in a 1920s villa with a garden on the border of Vinohrady and Vršovice. Behind the green gate with the number 63 you can barely hear the city and time slows down. The entrance is from Říčanská street; the nearest tram stop is Orionka (lines 10 and 16), and Flora metro is a short walk. Dogs, kids and cyclists are welcome.

Czech breakfast with a twist

The kitchen sticks to honest Czech classics and the menu changes with the seasons. Breakfast may include hemenex (ham and eggs), scrambled eggs with fried onion and chives, sausages with horseradish, a trio of spreads or sweet potato dumplings with poppy seeds. Open Wed–Sun 8:30–18:00; book online.
vila-63-praha.tip: On a nice day, sit in the villa garden and have a Czech breakfast – hemenex, scrambled eggs with fried onion or the spread trio. In autumn, don't miss the pumpkin spice latte.

misto-dejvice-praha.seoTitulek: Místo Dejvice Prague – breakfast café by Doubleshot
misto-dejvice-praha.seoPopis: Místo on Bubenečská, near Vítězné náměstí: café from the Doubleshot family with okonomiyaki, Turkish eggs, truffle omelette and plum French toast.
misto-dejvice-praha.popis:
Místo ("The Place") is a café and bistro on Bubenečská street in Dejvice, close to Vítězné náměstí. It belongs to the family of Doubleshot roastery and Můj šálek kávy, so great coffee is a given. The spacious wood-and-concrete interior is bright and works for breakfast with friends or a business meeting.

Breakfast with ideas

The menu mixes classics with world cuisines: Japanese okonomiyaki with bacon, egg and hoisin, Turkish eggs with spinach and savoury granola, an omelette with truffles and aged cheese, or bread with sautéed mushrooms and almond cream. Pastry comes from their own bakery. Open weekdays and Saturday from 9:00, Sunday from 10:00; book online.
misto-dejvice-praha.tip: Try the okonomiyaki with bacon and egg or the truffle omelette. For something sweet, the French toast with plums and tonka.

cafe-perfect-day-praha.seoTitulek: Café Perfect Day Prague – all-day breakfast in Dejvice
cafe-perfect-day-praha.seoPopis: Café Perfect Day on Kafkova, near Dejvická metro: bright café with all-day breakfast, cakes from its own Sweet Day patisserie and a summer terrace.
cafe-perfect-day-praha.popis:
Café Perfect Day is a café on Kafkova street in Dejvice, a few minutes' walk from Vítězné náměstí and Dejvická metro. Big windows, a bright interior and a street terrace in summer. A few house rules: no free wifi, no laptop work at weekends and no reservations – just drop in. Dogs welcome.

Breakfast all day

Breakfast is served all day, from morning till evening, alongside light lunches, soups and salads and small plates with wine. Desserts come from their own Sweet Day patisserie nearby. Open weekdays from 8:00, weekends from 9:00.
cafe-perfect-day-praha.tip: Breakfast runs all day, so have eggs with yoghurt and pita even in the afternoon – and pick a větrník, věneček or macarons from the Sweet Day counter.
